propositions: Pass-1 submits all chunks and agent futures concurrently to a 6-wide pool, causing N duplicate cache writes of the shared plan-bearing system prefix when the cache is cold, resulting in ~3.7x higher token consumption than optimal.

The warm-then-fan-out pattern successfully reduces redundant prefix writes by running a single call serially first to populate the cache, then fan-out the remainder to the pool, measured via per-call usage instrumentation.
When the estimated shared-prefix tokens are below CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS or fewer than 2 calls exist, the optimization is bypassed and behavior remains unchanged.
A non-systemic warm-call failure degrades gracefully to direct fan-out of the remainder; systemic LLMUnavailableError on the warm call aborts the review.
